exposure: pregnancy status (before, during trimesters, after pregnancy)
outcome: levels of 92 inflammation-related plasma proteins (e.g., PD-L1, LIF-R, TGF-b1, CCL28, CCL8, CCL13, CXCL5, TRANCE, TWEAK)
cohort: Fifteen multiple sclerosis patients and ten healthy controls were longitudinally sampled before, during, and after pregnancy.
finding: Gradual dynamic changes in plasma proteins, most prominent during the 3rd trimester and reverting post-partum, reflect the disease activity of multiple sclerosis during pregnancy, with upregulation of immunoregulatory proteins and downregulation of inflammatory chemokines.
